feature: Input-null predicate — `$p IS [NOT] NULL`, the optional filter that does not constrain when its input is null

scenarios.name: a supplied null widens the query and the optional filter leaves the plan entirely
scenarios.note: The demand shape: an optional `?zone=` filter that, unset, returns everything. All four fixture nodes come back. The load-bearing half is the SQL snapshot — a withdrawn filter must LEAVE THE PLAN, not lower as a no-op, so this snapshot carries no `dimensions` predicate at all and is the same plan the WHERE-less query emits. ORACLE SKIP, stated so nobody reads the green as differential coverage. `_fold_ast_param_predicates` runs inside the EXECUTOR, downstream of `parse_gryphon`, so the Gridkin runner hands model_oracle.py the UNFOLDED tree and `eval_predicate` ends at `raise OracleUnmodeled('predicate leaf ParamNullTest')`. That is a fail-closed skip, never a fake green: the envelope and SQL snapshots below are the only assertions running here. It closes the day the oracle grows a ParamNullTest branch.
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — no applicable feature folder (TAP-native: `$p IS NULL` is a predicate about an INPUT; openCypher has no parameter-existence predicate)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE $zone IS NULL OR n.dimensions.zone = $zone

scenarios.name: an absent param is still a hard error even when it is only ever null-tested
scenarios.note: The guard that makes the feature safe. Treating ABSENCE as null would silently widen the query to EVERYTHING whenever a caller forgot to wire the filter — the plausible, alarmless wrong answer. A param named in a query stays required; only a SUPPLIED None withdraws the filter. This scenario supplies no params at all, which is exactly the forgot-to-wire-it shape. VACUITY TRAP, measured and closed: `explain_gryphon_raw` wraps a GryphonParseError into a SearchExecutionError too, so with the whole `$p IS [NOT] NULL` grammar reverted this scenario still saw a SearchExecutionError and passed on the TYPE alone — a green that proved nothing. `message_contains` pins the required-inputs diagnostic specifically; do not relax it to the bare type.
